item: Whoever paid you already withheld the tax
value: Nothing.
note: The payer is the withholding agent. If it withheld and reported, the tax on that payment has been collected. How to tell: Download your Tax Payment Record (纳税记录). Each withheld payment appears on it.

item: The payer should have withheld and did not
note: The tax is collected from you. You had until 30 June of the year after you were paid, or the date in the tax office's notice. The payer can be fined 50% to 3 times the tax. How to tell: The payment is missing from your Tax Payment Record but the payer was a Chinese company or person.

item: Nobody was obliged to withhold
value: Surcharge of 0.05% a day from the next day, and a possible fine of 50% to 5 times the tax for not filing.
note: You had to file and pay within the first 15 days of the month after you were paid. How to tell: The payment is missing from your record and there was no withholding agent.

item: The money is not one of the nine taxable kinds of income
note: The law taxes nine listed kinds of income. Money that is none of them is outside this tax. How to tell: Compare each deposit with the list. Whether a gift or an inheritance falls outside it is still open on the dashboard (flags U07 and U08 there).

item: It is interest the bank paid on the deposit
value: No Chinese tax. U.S. tax at your own rate, with no Chinese tax to credit against it.
note: China has not collected tax on savings-deposit interest since 9 October 2008. The U.S. does tax it: it belongs on Form 1040 each year, and a foreign account means Schedule B, Part III. How to tell: Interest lines on the bank statement, year by year.

item: The tax itself
value: 20% of interest, dividends, rent, property-sale gains and incidental income. 3% to 45% on wages and fees, worked out per year.
note: For a property sale the tax base is the gain. For rent, 20% is deducted first (RMB 800 if the payment is RMB 4,000 or less).

item: Late-payment surcharge (滞纳金)
value: 0.05% of the unpaid tax for every day. 365 days comes to 18.25% of the tax.
note: Counted on the tax itself, from the day after the deadline to the day you pay.

item: The deadline the surcharge is counted from
value: Nobody obliged to withhold: the 15th of the month after you were paid. Payer failed to withhold: 30 June of the following year, or the date in the tax office's notice.

item: No surcharge when the tax office caused the shortfall
value: Tax only, and only three years back.
note: Applies when the office applied the law wrongly or acted unlawfully.

item: Surcharge when your payer failed to withhold
note: A 2004 reply says no surcharge is charged to either side. The 2018 law then gave the taxpayer a deadline of their own. Which one governs was not found.

item: Fine for never filing
value: 50% to 5 times the unpaid tax.
note: Added to the tax and the surcharge.

item: Fine for evasion
value: 50% to 5 times the unpaid tax, and prosecution if it amounts to a crime.
note: Evasion covers forged or hidden records, a false return, and refusing to file after the tax office told you to.

item: Fine for still not paying after an order
value: 50% to 5 times the unpaid tax, with enforced collection.

item: Fine on a payer who failed to withhold
value: 50% to 3 times the tax, charged to the payer.
note: The tax itself is still collected from you.

item: Filing late when no tax is unpaid
value: Up to RMB 2,000. RMB 2,000 to 10,000 in serious cases.

item: Which multiple between 0.5 and 5 applies
note: The law gives the range. The local tax office decides inside it.

item: How far back: calculation mistake
value: 3 years. 5 years when the shortfall adds up to RMB 100,000 or more.
note: Counted from the day the tax should have been paid. A calculation mistake means an unintended formula error or an obvious slip.

item: How far back: never filed
value: Generally 3 years. Up to 5 in special circumstances.
note: The 2009 reply says that not filing is not evasion. It does not define the special circumstances.

item: How far back: evasion
value: No limit.

item: Time limit on fines
value: No fine if the violation was not discovered within 5 years.
note: This limits the fine. The tax and surcharge follow the look-back rows above.

item: Whether the surcharge can grow past the tax itself
note: The collection law sets no ceiling. A separate law caps surcharges at the amount owed. No official text settling which applies to tax was read.

item: Prison
value: Up to 3 years for evading a relatively large amount that is 10% or more of the tax due. 3 to 7 years for a huge amount that is 30% or more.
note: Not pursued if, after the tax office's recovery notice, you pay the tax and the surcharge and have taken the administrative penalty. That protection is lost by anyone convicted of evasion, or fined for it twice or more by the tax authorities, in the previous five years. The amounts that count as large and huge were not read: F10.

item: Leaving China while tax is owed
value: The tax office can ask border control to stop you leaving.
note: Until the tax and surcharge are paid or a guarantee is given.

item: If you disagree with the assessment
value: Pay first, or give a guarantee. Then apply for review.

item: Chinese income tax you pay
value: Can be credited against U.S. tax on the same foreign income, up to a limit. Claimed on Form 1116.

item: Chinese surcharge and fines
value: Cannot be credited. Interest, fines and penalties paid to a foreign government are not taxes.

item: Which year the credit belongs to
value: The year you pay, for a cash-method taxpayer. Choosing the year the tax accrued is possible only on a timely original return, not an amended one, and then binds every later year.

item: Credit you cannot use in that year
value: Carried back 1 year, then forward 10 years.

item: How long you have to claim
value: 10 years to claim a refund when you paid more foreign tax than you had claimed.

item: Whether your credit lines up with the year the U.S. taxed the income
The income and the interest were on your returns, and the FBARs were filed
note: Nothing to fix. An FBAR is due for any year the foreign accounts together exceeded $10,000.

item: The income was reported and taxed, but FBARs were not filed
value: $0, as long as the IRS has not already contacted you about those years.
note: File the late FBARs online and give the reason they are late. The IRS's own page for this procedure could not be opened: F06.

item: The income was reported, but another international form is missing
value: Penalties may be assessed under the existing rules.
note: File it the normal way. Attach a reasonable-cause statement if you have one. Form 8938 and Form 3520 amounts are on the dashboard Tax page.

item: Income or interest was not reported, it was not willful, and you live outside the U.S.
value: $0 penalty. The tax and interest are still due.
note: Streamlined Foreign Offshore: 3 years of returns, 6 years of FBARs, Form 14653. Test: in at least one of the last three years you had no U.S. home and spent 330 full days outside the U.S.

item: Income or interest was not reported, it was not willful, and you live in the U.S.
value: 5% of the highest year-end total of the unreported foreign accounts, plus the tax and interest.
note: Streamlined Domestic Offshore: 3 years of amended returns, 6 years of FBARs, Form 14654. You must have filed a return for each of the last three years.

item: It was willful
note: IRS Criminal Investigation Voluntary Disclosure Practice, Form 14457. Revised terms were put out for comment on 22 December 2025. Final terms were not found.

item: You do nothing and the IRS finds it
value: 5% of the unpaid tax per month of late filing, up to 25%. 20% of underpaid tax. FBAR: up to $16,536 for each missed annual report, or for a willful case the greater of $165,353 or half the balance.
note: No procedure. No time limit on the tax if no return was filed. No FBAR penalty where there was reasonable cause and the balance was properly reported.

item: Interest on unpaid U.S. tax
value: 7% a year in the fourth quarter of 2026. Between 6% and 8% since 2024.
note: Runs from the original due date and accrues daily. An extension to file does not move the payment date.

item: When the streamlined procedures close
value: Once the IRS has opened an examination of any of your years.
note: They also need a signed statement that the failure was not willful.

item: How long the IRS has for the tax
value: 3 years after a return is filed. 6 years if more than $5,000 of income from reportable foreign assets was left out. No limit if no return was filed.

item: How long the IRS has for an FBAR penalty
value: 6 years.

item: How the non-willful FBAR penalty is counted
value: Once per missed annual report, not once per account.
